annotation.title_clean: Directive 2006/42/EC of the European Parliament and of the Council of 17 May 2006 on machinery, and amending Directive 95/16/EC (recast)
annotation.title_en: Directive 2006/42/EC of the European Parliament and of the Council of 17 May 2006 on machinery, and amending Directive 95/16/EC (recast)
annotation.authors_or_issuer: European Parliament and Council of the European Union
annotation.venue: Official Journal of the European Union, L 157
annotation.summary_en: The EU Machinery Directive 2006/42/EC (recast) sets essential health and safety requirements for machinery placed on the EU market. It requires risk assessment, CE marking, EC declarations of conformity, technical files, notified-body procedures for high-risk machinery and market surveillance. It is the baseline safety law for industrial robots and other machinery, though it contains no AI-specific provisions.
key_provisions_or_claims: Manufacturers must perform iterative risk assessment and meet Annex I essential health and safety requirements before placing machinery on the market.
Conformity assessment: internal checks for most machinery; EC type-examination or full quality assurance for Annex IV higher-risk machinery.
CE marking and EC declaration of conformity create a presumption of conformity; harmonised standards give a presumption of compliance.
Control systems must prevent hazardous situations from hardware/software faults, with emergency stop and safe start/stop requirements.
Member States must designate market surveillance authorities, notify conformity bodies and set effective, proportionate penalties; applicable from 29 December 2009.
